senses.gloss: उक्ष् [cf. Lith. ūkana: Hib. uisg, uisge, ‘water, a river’; uisgeach, ‘aquatic, watery, fluid, moist, pluvial:’ Gk. ὑγρός, ὑγρότης, ὑγραίνω: Lat. ūveo (for ugveo), ūmor, &c.]
2. उक्ष् mfn. ifc. dropping, pouring See बृहद्-उक्ष्
becoming strong See साकम्-उक्ष्.
उक्ष mfn. large, Nir.
ifc. = उक्ष॑न् below (see जातोक्ष, बृहद्-उक्ष, &c.)
उक्ष॑ (in comp. for उक्ष॑न्).
उक्षण n. sprinkling, consecrating, BhP.; VarBṛS.; Ragh. &c.
उक्षाण m. (= उक्षन्) a bull, R. (B.).

उक्षण्य Nom. P. उक्षण्य॑ति, to wish for bulls &c.;
to desire one who pours down riches [Sāy.], RV. viii, 26, 9.
उक्षण्या॑यन m. a descendant of Ukṣaṇya, RV. viii, 25, 22.
उक्षण्यु॑ mfn. wishing for bulls &c.
desirous of one who pours down riches [Sāy.], RV. viii, 23, 16.
उक्ष॑न् आ, m. an ox or bull (as impregnating the flock; in the Veda especially as drawing the chariot of Uṣas or dawn), RV.; AV.; TS.; KātyŚr.; MBh.; Kum. &c.
N. of the Soma (as sprinkling or scattering small drops)
of the Maruts
of the sun and Agni, RV.
one of the eight chief medicaments (ऋषभ), L.
N. of a man
उक्ष॑न् mfn. large, L.;
उक्षन् [cf. Zend ukhshan; Goth. auhsa and auhsu; Armen. eṣn.]
उक्ष—तर m. a small or young bull, Pāṇ. v, 3, 91
a big bull, L.
उक्ष—वश॑ m. sg. and du. a bull and a barren cow, TS.; ŚBr.
उक्ष—वेह॑त् m. an impotent bull, ŚBr.
उक्ष॑—सेन m. N. of a king, MaitrUp.
उक्षा॑न्न mfn. one whose food is oxen, RV. viii, 43, 11.
उक्षित॑ mfn. sprinkled, moistened, AV. v, 5, 8; MBh.; Ragh.; Kum. &c.
strong, of full growth, RV.
उक्ष्णोरन्ध्र m. N. of a Ṛṣi, TāṇḍBr.
